protocol.reference: Gillespie Glauber at h=0 for T_ref=1
protocol.actuation: site fields h_i=H0*target_spin_i switched instantaneously from 0 to target, then held fixed during Glauber T_ctrl=1
protocol.controller_no_info: target is exact Bayesian MAP state conditional on M_T; no access to X0
protocol.controller_with_info: target is actual X0; has access to all 16 initial spin values
protocol.paired: same sampled X0 and same uncontrolled X_T for both controllers; independent post-switch stochastic trajectories

memory_accounting.note: These are ideal Landauer lower bounds for resetting a memory register after use, not measured acquisition/storage work and not automatically additive to actuator work. Conditional reset assumes M_T remains available as side information. Actual memory architecture, measurement, writing, and reset protocol are not simulated.

limitations: This is a fixed-amplitude open-loop local-field protocol, not an optimized minimum-work controller.
The field is switched once and held; switching work is measured exactly from the pre-switch microstate, while no work is done during the hold.
The post-switch CTMC is sampled by Gillespie; confidence intervals quantify Monte Carlo uncertainty, not model uncertainty.
The no-information controller uses M_T only to choose a MAP target and does not observe X_T microstate.
The information controller is given X0 as a classical side-information register; its thermodynamic acquisition cost is not included.
